articles.title: I’ve always supported my dysfunctional siblings, but I’ve had enough. How can I divorce myself? | Annalisa Barbieri
articles.summary: You feel guilty because you’ve done ‘better’ in life, but you can’t rescue them. Listen to your resentment and learn to let go. I’m a 66-year-old widow and the middle of three siblings. They are struggling with mental health, financial issues, or both.
body: Recently, my older sister mistakenly texted me intimate pictures meant for the new man in her life. It’s one more disturbing thing in a very long line of disturbing things she’s said and done over the years and I’ve had enough. My world is so different from my siblings’ – it always has been.

I feel as if I’m carrying this family, but don’t feel a part of it. I never have, because my choices have always been different, even when we were children. Our parents are deceased, and I’ve become the de facto and very reluctant mother, I’m the responsible one. How can I divorce myself from them and not feel guilty? How can I shield myself from their dysfunction, and protect my own sense of peace? I know they will never change.

When one sibling seems to have a “better” life than the others, that can bring up guilt, and guilt is a strong tether to behaviours we’d rather not demonstrate. If you could get to the bottom of why you feel it’s your job to carry the family, it may help you start to unshackle yourself.
points: You feel guilty because you’ve done ‘better’ in life, but you can’t rescue them.
Listen to your resentment and learn to let go.
I’m a 66-year-old widow and the middle of three siblings.
It’s one more disturbing thing in a very long line of disturbing things she’s said and done over the years and I’ve had enough.

articles.title: Does your life feel out of control? Maybe you need some ‘pyt’ | Polly Hudson
articles.summary: This Danish concept encourages everyone to stop wasting energy on things we can’t change. You can even buy a pyt button to press. But does it help? We wouldn’t ignore tennis tips from Serena Williams, or culinary advice from Nigella Lawson, so when one of the happiest countries in the world lets…
body: Obligatory mention of hygge now dealt with, get ready to embrace “pyt”. Not to be confused with the 1983 Michael Jackson single, this Danish concept means accepting when a situation is out of our control. Then, even though we may be so angry and exasperated that we are in danger of spontaneous combustion, we don’t waste energy thinking any more about it and instead move on.

I might also decide to be taller, while I’m at it. Fluent in Japanese. The major shareholder in Amazon. My point is that while this is a theoretically sound idea, I’m not sure it works in practice. Simply making the choice to get over something and – ta-da! – it magically happens?

The approach works so well for the Danes that you can buy a pyt button to press when times become testing, and yet I remain sceptical. It feels as if we are veering dangerously towards toxic positivity territory.

Maybe the sticking point is that nine and three-quarter times out of 10, when we find ourselves experiencing a “daily hassle, frustration or mistake” it’s because we’re at the mercy of somebody else. Mind you, that means pyt could also be seen as forgiveness and awareness.
points: This Danish concept encourages everyone to stop wasting energy on things we can’t change.

articles.title: ‘Fabulous museums and no queues’: five of the best under-the-radar city breaks in Europe
articles.summary: From the Renaissance treasures of Parma to offbeat creativity in Nantes, these cities offer world-class art, great food and a laid-back alternative to Europe’s hotspots. As dilemmas go, it’s an unusual one: saddle up a giant squid or board a submersible for a voyage to the bottom of the ocean.
body: This is now the stomping ground of the Grand Éléphant, a 12m-high mechanical pachyderm that carries passengers on tours of the island, spraying bystanders with water from its trunk. I’d seen photos but nothing prepares you for the thrill of turning a corner and seeing the real thing lumbering towards you. You can learn about the magic behind the machinery at the nearby Galerie des Machines, where the creators bring a mechanical menagerie of strange creatures to life.

Just yards away, children are playing in the dancing water fountains of the square, while the white-aproned waiters of art nouveau brasserie La Cigale weave through the pavement tables delivering seafood platters to diners unfazed by the apocalyptic scene before them. Titled Fossil Opera, the artwork is a commentary on consumerism and the fleeting nature of human endeavour, and is one of about a dozen site-specific installations that have appeared in the city, as if by magic.

articles.title: ‘It was a sweet, tender voice’: the pilot who fell for his air traffic controller – before ever seeing her
articles.summary: Alfredo Bravo had a job he loved and was determined never to be grounded by marriage and kids. Then a voice from the control tower changed everything. Alfredo Bravo had landed aeroplanes in a lot of sticky situations – as a bush pilot in Chilean Patagonia and as a commercial pilot in rural China …
body: His first was that he was not Chilean. Bravo was born in Montevideo, Uruguay, a quietly functional socialist democracy with a mass middle class, an erudite populace, and a fleet of dilapidated motorcars – a bit like Cuba might have become had things worked out. Thus he avoided the vitriol directed towards the Chilean government for its three-centuries-long campaign of repression of Indigenous peoples.

Bravo’s second ace was his generous nature. On his days off, the young pilot began offering free flights, and spent his Saturdays and Sundays twirling local kids into the air. “Soon after, the community adopted me, they sent me food all the time,” says Bravo.

Bravo began to invent reasons to talk to the air traffic controllers. How could he match a face to that voice? It took him weeks. Pilots and air traffic controllers had mismatched schedules; controllers worked for three to five days, then had two or three days off. There were few routines, few fixed schedules.

articles.title: Amanda Seyfried, Susan Sarandon, Pamela Anderson, and More Joined Miu Miu for Venice Film Festival’s Most Glamorous Dinner
articles.summary: There are plenty of glitzy parties at Venice Film Festival, but none with quite the same sparkle as Miu Miu’s annual dinner at Fondazione Prada
body: Indeed, they may also be drawn to the party by the prospect of having an audience with Mrs. Prada herself: at the beginning of the evening, the designer could be seen in an embroidered tunic dress, sipping Champagne, and catching up with Pamela Anderson; as the evening progressed, she took her place for dinner at a table surrounded by Zhao, Luca Guadagnino, and Orlando Bloom, with Susan Sarandon later pulling up a pew to chat.

But the A-listers in town for the festival make a beeline for Miu Miu’s dinner, in particular, because it’s genuinely intimate. Taika Waititi was doing the rounds, catching up with Casey Affleck and sharing a spirited conversation with Amanda Seyfried; Emma Corrin and Zoey Deutch were happiest out on the balcony, enjoying the spectacular views down the Grand Canal as gondolas and water taxis zig-zagged across the shimmering black water below. It was enough to have everyone staying and sipping wine at their tables far past midnight—even those with panel talks and screenings the next morning. That’s how you know it’s a good party.

articles.title: Consciously Coupled: Owen Thiele and Jared Ellner on Working Side by Side and Being Gemini-for-Scorpio
articles.summary: The “Adults” star and his stylist partner—who’s dressed everyone from Sabrina Carpenter to Olivia Rodrigo to Thiele himself—have been dating since college.
body: It’s the age-old question that’s sparked a thousand romance novels and lovelorn midnight Google searches: how do you make a relationship work? Especially when both parties are very busy? In this column, we’ll be talking to some of our favorite star-for-star pairs about how they work together, inspire each other, and navigate love in the public eye.

It’s been a big summer for Owen Thiele, arguably the breakout star of the recently released second season of FX’s Adults. But things are no less busy for Thiele’s partner, Jared Ellner, a stylist known for dressing everyone from Sabrina Carpenter and Olivia Rodrigo to Emma Chamberlain.

Thiele and Ellner, who have been dating since college, some 11 years ago (“I dropped out two weeks after I got there, but in those two weeks, I met Jared Ellner, so it was worth the tuition,” jokes Thiele), and who live together in Los Angeles, are linked by more than romance: Ellner is also Thiele’s stylist. So it’s safe to say the two have learned quite a bit over the years about how to balance work and love.
points: The “Adults” star and his stylist partner—who’s dressed everyone from Sabrina Carpenter to Olivia Rodrigo to Thiele himself—have been dating since college.

articles.title: At Venice Film Festival, Amal Clooney and Emma Corrin Joined a Star-Studded Toast to the Cartier Cinema Club
articles.summary: The stars—including Chloé Zhao, Kate Mara, and Orlando Bloom—stepped out to celebrate Cartier’s fifth year as the main sponsor of the Venice Film Festival at the Gritti Palace last night.
body: Che bello! On Friday night, a glittering cast of film and fashion talents elegantly made their way onto the dock of the Gritti Palace from an army of grumbling water taxis, ready to celebrate Cartier ’s fifth year as main sponsor of the Venice Film Festival —and the launch of the fine jewelry house’s brand-new Cartier Cinema Club.

But most of all, it was an opportunity for many of the biggest stars whose films are premiering this week, as well as some of the jury members—including composer Daniel Blumberg and his girlfriend, Taylor Russell—to sit back, sip a negroni, catch up with friends, and watch the reflection of the grand Santa Maria della Salute church on the opposite bank shimmering in the black waters of the Grand Canal. That’s why Venice is often referred to as the most glamorous film festival in the world.

articles.title: The Best On-Court Style Moments Served at the 2026 U.S. Open
articles.summary: The 2026 U.S. Open is in full swing! With Naomi Osaka, Coco Gauff, and Venus Williams in play, don’t expect traditional tennis whites on the hard court.
body: Ready, set…style. The 2026 U.S. Open is in full swing in Queens, New York City, with the season already serveing up some thrilling,—and stylish—moments.

Serena Williams made her return with doubles partner Carlos Alcaraz, who was back in it after an injury that struck him out of this year’s Wimbledon. The duo sported some striking matching royal purple and black Nike kits. Roger Federer played a once-in-a-lifetime exhibition match at the Arthur Ashe Stadium with Lorenzo Musetti—and also launched a limited-edition version of On’s The Roger shoe —before absconding to Rhode Island to be inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame.

Across the next few days, we’ll see the likes of women’s world number one Aryna Sabalenka, Naomi Osaka, Coco Gauff, Venus Williams, Taylor Fritz, and more hit the Flushing Meadows hard court. The Williams sisters were at the forefront of subverting traditional tennis whites. Gauff debuted her latest New Balance x Miu Miu on the London grass, while Sabalenka is a Gucci face, Fritz is a Boss ambassador, and Novak Djokovic reps Lacoste.
points: With Naomi Osaka, Coco Gauff, and Venus Williams in play, don’t expect traditional tennis whites on the hard court.
